Getting started with psnr

Source: vignettes/psnr.Rmd
psnr.Rmd

psnr generates the sampling lists for collecting cognitive social structures data: for each person (the perceiver), a stratified set of real and counterfactual relationships in their social orbit. It calls the Julia package SamplingPerceivedNetworks.jl, which is documented at https://human-nature-lab.github.io/SamplingPerceivedNetworks.jl; read its guide for the procedure itself. This vignette shows the R calls. It needs Julia (1.10 or later) and is only evaluated when Julia is found.

Setup

The first time, psn_setup() creates a Julia environment for psnr and installs the Julia package into it (a few minutes). The other functions call it automatically afterwards.

library(psnr)
psn_setup()
library(psnr)

A network

A network is a table of ties, one row per tie. Names can be numbers or strings; they are converted to character.

set.seed(1)
g <- igraph::sample_smallworld(1, 100, 3, 0.2)
igraph::V(g)$name <- paste0("p", seq_len(igraph::vcount(g)))
edges <- igraph::as_data_frame(g, what = "edges")
head(edges, 3)
#>   from  to
#> 1   p1  p2
#> 2   p3  p9
#> 3   p4 p76

Lists for every perceiver

With no design given, psn_sample() uses the design fielded in Honduras: for each of degrees 1 to 4, five real and five counterfactual pairs.

lists <- psn_sample(edges, nodes = igraph::V(g)$name)
#> Julia version 1.13.1 at location /opt/hostedtoolcache/julia/1.13.1/x64/bin will be used.
#> Loading setup script for JuliaCall...
#> Warning in system2(file.path(.julia$bin_dir, "julia"), shQuote(command), :
#> running command ''/opt/hostedtoolcache/julia/1.13.1/x64/bin/julia'
#> '--startup-file=no'
#> '/home/runner/work/_temp/Library/JuliaCall/julia/install_dependency.jl'
#> '/opt/R/4.6.1/lib/R' 2>&1' had status 139
#> Finish loading setup script for JuliaCall.
head(lists)
#>   perceiver from  to bin  real
#> 1       p19  p13 p30   3  TRUE
#> 2       p19  p20 p79   2  TRUE
#> 3       p19  p25 p92   3 FALSE
#> 4       p19  p24 p66   3  TRUE
#> 5       p19 p100 p11   4  TRUE
#> 6       p19  p18 p21   1  TRUE
table(lists$bin, lists$real)
#>    
#>     FALSE TRUE
#>   1   486  226
#>   2   514  774
#>   3   500  500
#>   4   500  500

The result is reproducible with set.seed(), or with the seed argument.

To check or merge with the true network, note that each pair is sorted alphanumerically in the same way in lists:

truth <- with(edges, paste(pmin(from, to), pmax(from, to)))
mean(paste(lists$from, lists$to)[lists$real] %in% truth)
#> [1] 1

A different design

desired has one row per bin (real, counterfactual) and dvals lists the degrees in each. Consecutive degrees in one element, like 1:2, are merged into a single bin:

merged <- psn_sample(
  edges,
  desired = rbind(c(10, 10), c(5, 5), c(5, 5)),
  dvals = list(1:2, 3, 4)
)
unique(merged$bin)
#> [1] "1:2" "3"   "4"

Consents

consents is a named vector of codes (0 = none, 1 = survey only, 2 = survey and photo, 3 = photo only), with an entry for every node. Perceivers with code 1 or 2 receive a list, and pairs are limited to people with code 2 or 3.

codes <- setNames(sample(0:3, 100, replace = TRUE, prob = c(.1, .2, .5, .2)),
                  igraph::V(g)$name)
with_consent <- psn_sample(edges, consents = codes)
length(unique(with_consent$perceiver))
#> [1] 68

Inclusion probabilities

psn_inclusion_probs() returns the exact probability, pi, that each pair is on a perceiver’s list, with the same design arguments. Its inverse is the weight for estimation.

probs <- psn_inclusion_probs(edges)
probs$weight <- 1 / probs$pi
head(probs)
#>   perceiver from  to bin real        pi   weight
#> 1        p1 p100  p3   1 TRUE 1.0000000 1.000000
#> 2        p1   p3  p5   2 TRUE 0.2727273 3.666667
#> 3        p1   p3  p9   2 TRUE 0.2727273 3.666667
#> 4        p1   p4  p5   2 TRUE 0.2727273 3.666667
#> 5        p1   p4 p76   2 TRUE 0.2727273 3.666667
#> 6        p1   p4 p92   2 TRUE 0.2727273 3.666667
